purpose: Product-pattern benchmark for EcoReport's AI-assisted investment research workflow.

sources.name: Bloomberg AI / ASKB
sources.observedPattern: Agentic research coordinates multiple data/news/research agents, gives transparent attribution, and exposes underlying query logic when data analysis is included.
sources.ecoreportRule: Every action-facing claim must remain traceable through claim id, evidence ids, source audit map, and deterministic quality flags.

sources.name: AlphaSense Generative Search / Generative Grid
sources.observedPattern: Repeatable multi-document prompts are rendered as table-like grids, with one-click citations and follow-up questions over broker reports, calls, filings, and internal content.
sources.ecoreportRule: Turn the 100-report daily corpus into reusable claim/atom tables first; use Deep Research only for narrow follow-up questions and source verification.

sources.name: Fiscal.ai
sources.observedPattern: AI summaries sit beside financial data, KPIs, dashboards, notifications, investor relations content, and click-through auditability.
sources.ecoreportRule: Keep human reports, execution strategy, AI packets, and source audit files separate but linked by the same date/run id.

sources.name: Koyfin
sources.observedPattern: Portfolio, watchlist, macro dashboard, transcript search, ETF/fund coverage, and customizable visual workflows are treated as one research surface.
sources.ecoreportRule: Final outputs must connect macro, sector, holdings, watchlist/new-candidate, ETF mapping, and account-level actions in one daily decision surface.

sources.name: The Transcript AI
sources.observedPattern: Earnings-call analysis is decomposed into executive summary, key metrics, management tone, guidance, strategic signals, red flags, Q&A dynamics, and uncertainty-aware rankings.
sources.ecoreportRule: Do not stop at consensus summary; preserve red flags, minority views, uncertainty, Q&A/analyst-reaction style objections, and confidence bands.

sources.name: AlphaVistaAI
sources.observedPattern: Multiple specialist agents combine technical, fundamental, sentiment, real-time data tools, portfolio diversification, and tailored investor profile insights.
sources.ecoreportRule: Separate specialist contexts for research, portfolio action, claim review, and source audit; then recombine only after quality gates.

sources.name: The Motley Fool investor survey
sources.observedPattern: Investors use generative AI most for stock research, market-trend analysis, news/filing summarization, portfolio management, and time savings, while accuracy/privacy remain major concerns.
sources.ecoreportRule: Prioritize time-saving triage, but keep accuracy/privacy guardrails: no raw personal account data in external prompts unless explicitly intended and minimized.

sources.name: FINRA AI / investment fraud guidance
sources.observedPattern: Warnings focus on guaranteed returns, unrealistic AI trading claims, high-pressure tactics, pump-and-dump risk, and misleading AI-related promotion.
sources.ecoreportRule: Block guaranteed-return language, hype-only catalysts, high-pressure action wording, and weak-evidence BUY exposure.

dailyResearchLenses.question: Which claims affect action, and can each be traced to source ids without relying on long prose?
Can today's reports be compared by the same columns: thesis, catalyst, risk, evidence, confidence, portfolio impact?
Which holdings, watchlist names, and candidate sectors changed today versus yesterday?
What would make the top thesis wrong, and which reports disagree?
Which actions survive evidence, category concentration, confidence, and account fit checks?

researchContext: Preserve non-consensus claims, minority views, red flags, and uncertainty separately from consensus.
Represent repeatable review columns as compact arrays rather than narrative paragraphs.
Never merge multiple brokers into a single claim unless evidenceIds show source diversity.
portfolioActionContext: Expose validated buys only; keep rejected candidates visible as research backlog, not recommendations.
Show account fit, allocation gap, concentration risk, and timing condition separately.
Treat macro/sector/watchlist monitoring as separate lenses before final action.
claimReviewContext: Review only risky claims, guaranteed-return wording, weak evidence, pump-like language, and hype-only catalysts.
Allowed decisions are retain, soften, hold, remove.
Prefer softer claims when the direction is plausible but evidence is thin.
sourceAuditMap: Keep raw text out of the packet; use source ids, titles, broker, category, ticker, and claim links.
Make one-hop audit possible from every action-facing claim to source ids.
